advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either wire SOURCES/CONFIDENCES into validation and import them in the heldout test, or remove the unused frozensets and rely on a single source of truth.
evidence: search: SOURCES defined at registry.py:38 with no other usage in src/rebar/metrics
search: CONFIDENCES defined at registry.py:41, used only via a duplicated literal `_CONFIDENCES = {"high", "classified"}` at test_registry_heldout.py:32
SOURCES/CONFIDENCES are not in registry.__all__ nor re-exported by src/rebar/metrics/__init__.py:25-32
advisory.finding: SOURCES and CONFIDENCES frozensets are defined but never referenced by any code path (only AUTHORITATIVE_SOURCES is used); the heldout test re-declares the same tokens as local literals (_SOURCES/_CONFIDENCES) instead of importing the module constants, so the vocabulary and its test copy can drift out of sync.
scenarios: A new source token is added to SOURCES in registry.py but the test's _SOURCES literal is not updated (or vice versa); the vocabulary check passes/fails against a stale set.
advisory.suggested_fix: Import SOURCES/CONFIDENCES in test_registry_heldout.py and assert against them instead of the duplicated _SOURCES/_CONFIDENCES literals; and reference them in MetricSpec validation so they are not dead constants.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion that evaluate() returns MetricValue with metric_id equal to the spec's id.
evidence: registry.py:117-122 sets `metric_id=spec.id` on the returned MetricValue
test_data_yields_metric_value_carrying_labels asserts only `result.value`, `result.source`, `result.confidence` (test_registry.py:72-76) — metric_id is never asserted here or in the heldout suite
ABSENCE: evaluate() could return metric_id=None or metric_id=spec.source and every test still passes
registry.py:112 `if result is None:` — dispatch keys on identity-None, not falsiness
test_no_data_yields_unavailable uses `compute=lambda ctx: None` (test_registry.py:62); test_data_yields_metric_value uses `compute=lambda ctx: 42` (test_registry.py:70) — no falsy-non-None case
ABSENCE: a compute returning 0 must yield MetricValue(value=0); changing the guard to `if not result` would break this behavior with no failing test
advisory.finding: No test asserts that evaluate() populates MetricValue.metric_id with the spec's id, despite metric_id being documented public surface set at registry.py:121.
merged_from: The evaluate() dispatch distinguishes None from falsy values via `if result is None`, but no test exercises a falsy-but-not-None compute result (0, '', False, []); a regression to `if not result` would misroute real data to Unavailable undetected.

Only the REGISTRY seed entries are vocabulary-checked (test_registry_heldout.py:65-68); arbitrary MetricSpec constructions are not constrained
dropped.finding: The 'closed' provenance vocabularies (SOURCES, CONFIDENCES) are documented as closed and defined as frozensets, but MetricSpec construction and evaluate() perform no validation — a MetricSpec with an out-of-vocabulary source/confidence is accepted and its labels ride into MetricValue unchecked.
scenarios: A later ticket adds a spec with source='backfilled' (typo) or confidence='medium'; it flows through evaluate() into a MetricValue and is treated as valid data.
dropped.suggested_fix: Add a __post_init__ to MetricSpec that asserts `source in SOURCES` and `confidence in CONFIDENCES`, raising ValueError with the offending value.
